claims.text: Predictions can be made approximately fair with respect to multiple possible causal models simultaneously.
Learning a fair classifier under multiple competing causal explanations can be framed as an optimization problem with fairness constraints.
The optimization problem for learning fair classifiers under competing causal models can be solved using gradient-based methods.

evidence.description: In this paper, we show how it is possible to make predictions that are approximately fair with respect to multiple possible causal models at once, thus mitigating the problem of exact causal specification.
We frame the goal of learning a fair classifier as an optimization problem with fairness constraints entailed by competing causal explanations.
We show how this optimization problem can be efficiently solved using gradient-based methods.

methodologies.name: Multi-world counterfactual fairness optimization
methodologies.description: Formulates fair classification across competing causal models as a constrained optimization problem solved using gradient-based optimization.

limitations.text: Standard counterfactual fairness methods require specification of the exact causal model that generated the data, which cannot be fully validated without further assumptions.
The proposed method achieves predictions that are approximately fair across multiple causal models, rather than exact fairness.
